findings: Dashboard operators on a supporting plan can choose one of three risk presets or set a custom Fraudulent dispute threshold with backtesting. A nonmatching threshold puts the account in Manual mode. The modal projects fraud blocked and payments accepted from four months of data.

Enabling a risk setting disables the default high-risk score block rule and it cannot be re-enabled. Custom rules remain separate. The classic risk score remains available as a custom-rule attribute with plan eligibility.

Adaptive 3DS uses ML to authenticate medium-risk payments. Issuers may challenge and liability typically shifts on successful 3DS for fraud-related disputes. Regulatory/SCA-required 3DS can still activate when adaptive 3DS is off; the fraud-prevention control is unavailable in sandboxes.

November expands the risk-level description: Normal does not guarantee legitimacy, Elevated indicates more signals without establishing fraud, and Highest indicates the strongest signals. The distinction between the Dashboard aggregate and the classic-risk rules attribute remains (old raw lines 74-80 and new raw lines 103-113).
substantive_changes: November adds Fraudulent card payments at Standard and above, using the separate card-only 0–99 fraudulent payment score to cover likely fraud even if disputes or early fraud warnings are unlikely. Custom rule access for that score is plan-qualified.

November documents a card-only dynamic threshold that temporarily blocks additional elevated and high-risk payments under detected fraud pressure, restores the default when the threat ceases, and respects a manually configured threshold when that threshold blocks more. The separately reviewed November plan matrix lists transaction risk scores, risk preferences, custom rules and Adaptive 3DS for Plus/Pro and dynamic thresholds for Pro (raw/stripe-radar-how-radar-works-2026-11-07.md:26-46).

Early fraud warning becomes documented for Balanced as well as Maximize protection. Non-card controls use supported payment methods wording. Custom Fraudulent dispute and score-rule instructions omit historical Fraud Teams-specific text, while plan qualification remains and no old-to-new plan equivalence is established.

November adds direct-charge configuration for connected accounts controlled solely by the platform, with connected-account only, platform only or shared management. Shared evaluates a single rule set starting with platform rules and preserves action ordering, including allow overriding block in either account direction. In the specified Lite or platform-only cases, Dashboard visibility allows outcomes view-only.
